title: Set four M3 heat-set inserts flush and square in a printed robot bracket with a soldering iron and a flat block
instruction: Set the four inserts flush and square into the bracket with the soldering iron and the flat block, then put the iron back in its stand.
context: Printed parts of robots (gripper fingers, joint housings, sensor brackets) take their screws in brass heat-set inserts, set with a soldering iron and an insert tip, then a flat piece of metal pressed on each while the plastic is still hot, to seat the last bit flush and square. A robot building robots does this many times per part. The insert sinks only while the plastic round it is soft: light steady pressure for a few seconds, the iron square to the hole, stopping just short of flush; then, within seconds, the iron cleared and the block pressed on it level. Pushed hard it ends loose; leaning, crooked; past flush the hot shoulder marks the part; the block too late does nothing. The iron is hot and goes back into a sloping holder tube.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left). Blue silicone soldering mat (2 mm, 20 x 16 cm) at (27, -4.5). On it, an orange PETG bracket 80 x 40 x 12 mm (STL and drawing in README: four 4.0 mm holes 7 mm deep, 56 x 20 mm apart), long side along y, centred at (28, -8). In each hole a brass CNC Kitchen M3 standard insert (M3 x 5.7 mm, 4.6 mm OD), dropped in, top about 4.5 mm proud. A flat block (6061 aluminium square bar 19 x 19 mm, a 50 mm offcut with faced ends, 49 g) stands on its end on the mat at (22, 0.5). Hakko FX-888D station at 245 C (unit off the table), iron with an M3 heat-set tip (Hakko T18 fit, e.g. Adafruit 4239) resting tip down in its holder: weighted base clamped to the table, tube 30 mm inside, 9 cm long, sloping 50 degrees down away from the arms, closed end at (42, -27), 3 cm up. Arms in the ready pose.
scoring: 0 if at any time the iron's tip or barrel touched the robot (real trial: came within 2 cm, e-stop), or the iron was out of its stand and in no grip for 2 s, or at the end it is not resting in its stand, released. Otherwise per insert: 0.25 if its top is within 0.5 mm of the face and it was pressed flat with the block within 3 s of the iron leaving it (straightedge across it both ways: no 0.5 mm feeler under it, no 0.1 mm feeler beside the insert, i.e. no raised lip; video for the timing); 0.10 if seated but not that (0.5 to 2.5 mm proud, 0.5 to 1 mm sunk, or flush with the lip left: no block or too late); 0 if higher, or crooked (sunk with iron or block leaning over 5 deg: a hand-threaded M3 x 12 screw stands over 1 mm off a try square), forced (pushed over 15 N while sinking: the insert turns when the screw is tightened), or next to a melt mark (hot iron on the face 0.5 s: photo). Success 1.0: all four flush and pressed flat, iron in its stand, 1 s.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (2 minutes at 20 Hz); the scripted demo needs about 1,760
reset_notes: Each trial uses a fresh printed bracket and four new inserts (dropped into the holes by hand). Put the iron back in its stand with a heat-resistant glove if needed; the station stays on at 245 C. Seeds (HSI_SEED) set each insert's start height (4.2 to 4.8 mm proud) and the bracket's softness in the simulation.
fidelity: Approximate. PhysX cannot melt plastic: a rule moves each insert. It sinks only after 2.5 s of the iron pressing on it, then at 0.3 mm/s per N above 1.5 N (+-25% by seed). Within 3 s of the iron leaving, the block sinks the last 1.5 mm the same way, stops at flush and flattens the lip. Over 15 N: forced; leaning over 5 deg: crooked; iron on the bracket 0.5 s: melt mark. Values estimated; README gives how to measure them.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; scripted demo: 1.0 (seed 0; also 1.0 on seeds 4 and 10)
